criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`. In the generated index.html under target/site, the Limits of this study finding ids are consecutive, or the page states why f2 is missing. Check by grep.

The policy hook would not let me Grep that file because it is outside the working directory, so I did not grep the built file. Instead I relied on tests that call the same `render` on the real study data. Both passed: the new `the_real_pages_limits_list_has_consecutive_finding_ids` (ids == 1..=n) and the existing `xtask/tests/site_page.rs::the_rendered_page_has_the_newcomer_fixes` (ids == [f1,f2,f3]). findings.json at HEAD has ids f1, f2, f3.

criteria.criterion: In the generated index.html, the text 'Its study id, firstmate-work-handling' is absent from the header. If it is kept, it appears after the Claims and sources content.
criteria.evidence:
In site.rs lines 259-273 the header has no study id. The study id is only in the 'About this page' section (line 568), which renders after 'Claims and sources'. The passing tests assert that `!html[..].contains("study id")` and that the note's offset is greater than the offset of `

Claims and sources

`.

criteria.criterion: In the generated index.html, a one-sentence plain description of firstmate with a claim link appears before the 'Words used first' heading. Check the byte offsets with grep.
criteria.evidence:
intro.json `what_is` is a single sentence: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker, ...". It cites c1, c11, c21 and c22. site.rs line 287 renders it directly before `

Words used first

`. The passing tests compare the byte offsets (what_is < Words used first) and check for href="#claim-c1" in that span. I could not grep the built file (outside the working directory), so the offsets come from the tests.

criteria.evidence: The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, docs/design/explainer-site.md and xtask/src/site.rs, all on the deliverables list. intro.json and findings.json are not changed because the base already held the fixes. No out-of-scope file changed.

findings.summary: The new CHANGELOG entry repeats an existing Unreleased entry and uses process jargon a stranger can't follow
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md line 259 (already in the base, under [Unreleased]) records the same four fixes and their tests. The new entry at lines 12-18 sits under 'Fixed' but fixes nothing. It says 'The base already renders all four fixes', and 'the base' means nothing to an outside reader. A one-line 'Added: a test that...' entry, or no entry, would be clearer.

findings.summary: The new test mostly repeats an existing check
findings.evidence: xtask/tests/site_page.rs::the_rendered_page_has_the_newcomer_fixes (lines 169-177) already asserts that the finding ids are [f1,f2,f3] on the real page. The new unit test generalises this to 1..=n, which adds little.

findings.summary: I could not grep the built index.html directly
findings.evidence: `cargo run -p xtask -- site` wrote to CARGO_TARGET_DIR/site/index.html, outside the working directory. The policy hook denied Grep on that path. The behavior criteria were checked instead through the passing tests that render the same real study with the same `render` function.

summary: The candidate passes, but the four fixes were already on the page before this change. The base renders f1, f2 and f3 consecutively, keeps the study id out of the header and shows it after the claims, has a one-sentence cited definition of firstmate before "Words used first", and puts `./setup.sh` and `athena ask "add a changelog"` in Next steps. The base also already had tests for all of this and a changelog entry for it (CHANGELOG.md line 259). The producer saw this correctly and left the study data alone. The change adds a unit test for consecutive finding ids, a note in the design doc, and a new changelog entry. I checked the criteria through the passing `cargo test -p xtask` run, which renders the real study, and by reading site.rs and the study JSON. I couldn't grep the built index.html because it is written outside the working directory and the policy hook denied it. Athena's records show fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed. Every criterion is met and nothing is out of scope. Two minor findings: the new changelog entry repeats the existing one, sits under "Fixed" when it fixes nothing, and says "the base", which a stranger can't follow; and the new test mostly repeats a check in xtask/tests/site_page.rs.
